tools.name: search_pairs
tools.description: Discover supported crypto, equity, FX, and metal symbols before using the paid HTTP API. Returns up to 50 catalog matches with asset class, available services, and pricing tier; it is free, read-only, and never returns live prices or starts payment.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: List the supported instruments for one Blocksize service. This is free, read-only catalog metadata; it does not fetch live prices, create accounts, or start x402 payment.

tools.name: get_pricing_info
tools.description: Inspect current per-call prices, bulk credit tiers, and supported Solana and Base USDC settlement networks. This is free and read-only planning metadata; it does not initiate payment.

tools.name: get_product_catalog
tools.description: Inspect Blocksize raw data, supported equity ticker bid/ask, and premium agent-native workflow products, including starter-credit positioning, credit costs, suggested paid prices, endpoint templates, and upgrade path. This is free and read-only.

tools.name: get_workflow_endpoint
tools.description: Build the exact paid HTTP endpoint, method, starter-credit cost, and example body for a premium Blocksize workflow. This is free and read-only; it does not fetch live data, charge credits, or start x402.

tools.name: get_market_data_endpoint
tools.description: Build the exact x402-protected HTTP URL for one live market-data request. Returns method, URL, service notes, pricing docs, and next steps; it is read-only and does not fetch prices, charge a wallet, or submit payment.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Blocksize documentation and catalog metadata by keyword. This free read-only search returns document and instrument ids for fetch; it does not return live prices or start payment.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one document or instrument guide returned by search. This is free, read-only content retrieval with no account, credential, payment, or live-price side effects.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_pairs" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Discover supported crypto, equity, FX, and metal symbols before using the paid HTTP API. Returns up to 50 catalog matches with asset class, available services, …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "server" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_market_data_endpoint · Private data: get_market_data_endpoint, search, fetch · Public sink: get_market_data_endpoint.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_market_data_endpoint · Private data: get_market_data_endpoint, search, fetch · Public sink: get_market_data_endpoint

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
